official.note: Rockstar’s page lists PS5 and Xbox Series X|S with a 19 November 2026 date and does not mention PC. Rockstar’s Newswire and Take-Two’s news page could not be read today; press on 27 November reports no announcement.

repos.note: Read repository metadata for every listed project through the GitHub API and the READMEs of the 24 that had new commits.

discovery.note: Compared the list with PortWatch VI and GTA 6 PC Race and searched GitHub. Added foxhound and Vilocity. Left out cool_fox copies and small forks that publish no measurement of their own.

dmca.note: GitHub has published no Take-Two notice since 24 November. The newest notice in the November folder is unrelated.

press.note: Read TechRadar, TweakTown, Make Tech Easier, TechPowerUp, Tom’s Hardware and IGN from 26 and 27 November.

ps5.note: Read KytyPS5’s issue tracker and roadmap thread and AnyPS5’s discussions. Users of both report GTA VI starting, without a usable picture. shadPS4 has nothing for it.

safety.note: Read Bitdefender’s 26 November report on two fake repositories, plus the earlier NordVPN kit and 355-domain reports.

gdk.note: Searched press, GitHub and both trackers for a leak of Microsoft’s console kit. Found one unsourced Reddit post and nothing that confirms it. Read DexNom’s public code, the November notices and the SDK rules in XCL, VIctory, OpenEra and BetterXen.

gaps: Frame rates come from different scenes, settings and graphics cards, so they are not directly comparable. Each figure links to where it was published.

Most figures are the projects’ own. “Self-reported” means only the project’s README says so, “Tracker” means another tracker reports having seen or checked the build, and “Press” means a named outlet covered it.
Private builds have no public code. Their entries rely on PortWatch VI.
Dozens of smaller VIctory forks exist. The list keeps the ones with a distinct approach, a measured result or press coverage.
